items.t: Chapter 6 (al-bāb al-sādis): On spiritual retreat (khalwa) and what pertains specially to the practitioners of the devotional seclusions (iʿtikāf) that give access to the celestial realms [75]

Know — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that by this chapter, mighty in import, one attains to the name al-ʿAzīz al-Raḥmān (the Mighty, the All-Merciful). A certain one of the righteous, of the imams of the religion, made devotional seclusion (iʿtikāf) in the preaching-chamber of the congregational mosque of Aleppo. It was like a grave, having in it no opening for the light except from the door; so when the door was shut, it remained like a grave, in narrowness and in darkness. He would pray with the congregation, and would go out backwards at the time of the standing for prayer; and when the prayer was finished, he would enter in his [former] state, facing the qibla, and would not look at anyone. /fol. 39v./ And the greater part of his humble entreaty and of his asking of God, mighty and exalted, at all his times, was that God should teach him the Greatest Name. And while he was thus one night, seated, striving earnestly in fervent supplication to God, exalted is He, with the litany of remembrance (dhikr), lo, there was a tablet of light that had taken form before his eyes, and upon it figures depicted. He turned away from it, lest looking at it should divert him from his turning toward God, exalted is He. Then he was struck with it in the face, and it was said to him: "Take what will profit you." Thereupon he opened his eyes and turned to the tablet, contemplating it.

And behold, it was four lines: a line above, a line below, a line on the right, and a line on the left; and in the middle a circle; and inside the circle another circle; and between the two circles the measure of a gap (fatḥa). And in the middle of the small circle is a line that cuts it into two halves; and in the upper half is the meeting of two other lines with the cutting line, [forming] a triangular figure; and written in the middle of it, from the pole of the circle: Nay, rather He is God (unidentified quotation; not a Qurʾānic verse); and a jīm in the angle of the two lines. And on the end of the right-hand line that meets the diameter of the circle is the letter dāl; and written near the letter is the name al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge), its beginning from the line of the triangle and its end close to the circle. And at the angle of the diameter from the circle is the letter alif; and the name al-Wāḥid (the One), exalted is He, is in front of the name al-Ṣamad, and behind it the name al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing), and behind the name al-Qahhār, behind it; and al-Qahhār is at the top of the line from the circle. And from inside the line — I mean the line of the triangle — is the letter yāʾ; and on the end of the left-hand line that meets the diameter of the circle is the letter hāʾ; and on the diameter, from the angle upon the line that meets the circle, are the name al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful) and the name al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), from the line of the triangle to the circle; and behind it the name al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving). And within the triangle, upon the diameter, is the letter ṭāʾ. And the lower half, upon the diameter, is a line of a quarter of the circle: a letter khāʾ added upon its diameter, a quarter of the circle, running to the circle; and another line issuing from it that ends at the half of the circle; and within this line is written mutajallī ("manifesting"); and within the other line from the diameter is written in light, at its end that faces the circle, the letter zāy. And outside this line, which is a quarter of the circle, is written qad atāka ("there has come to you"). And on the left half of the half-circle — that is, its quarter — are two lines: in one of them, namely the one that adjoins mutajallī, is written mukhtār ("chosen"); and in the other line is written bi-l-hudā ("with guidance"); and outside it is written ʿabd lanā ("a servant of Ours"). And from inside the other two lines, up to the half of the circle, is written the wāw; and there is written Those are ten complete (Q 2:196), running to the half of the pole. And written at the head of this diameter, upon the outer circle, is Alif-Lām-Mīm. God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 3:1–2), in disconnected letters. And this Alif-Lām-Mīm faces the jīm that is inside the triangle; and the lām-alif of lā ilāha illā huwa ("there is no god but He") faces the alif that is at the end of the pole on the left side; and al-Ḥayy faces the letter wāw that is at the bottom of the circle; and the mīm of al-Qayyūm faces Alif-Lām-Mīm. And the lines whose mention has already been made are before you. And the circle, at its edge, has written on the outside and God encompasses them round about (Q 85:20); and on the other side, outside the circle, is written Nay, it is a glorious Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:21–22). And in the lower line, outside the circle: Those who have denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers — they shall come to know (Q 40:70). And when I had firmly fixed its form in my mind well, by means of the figure, the form vanished from me. Then, when I had prayed the dawn prayer and had sat down, I began the recitation /fol. 40r./ of my litany (wird), and a drowsiness of sleep came over me. And while I was asleep I saw in it the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib — may God, exalted is He, ennoble his face and be pleased with him — and he said to me: "Where is the tablet that you were given?" And it was [still] depicted with me; so I handed it to him, and he deemed it mighty. And he said to me concerning its meaning things which I did not understand, nor did I grasp of them anything save a single word. That was that the Commander of the Faithful placed his finger upon the letter jīm that is in the angle of the triangle in the upper half of the circle, and said: "From Huwa ('He') the Name of Majesty issues forth." So I knew that it was the Greatest Name of God, and that the names point to it, and that it points to the transcendence (tanzīh) of the names of the holy Essence.

So I said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, I have not understood what you have said to me." He said to me: "Muḥammad b. Ṭalḥa will expound it to you, if God, exalted is He, wills." Then I awoke and completed my litany, and went to Ibn Ṭalḥa — for between me and him there was a covenant of brotherhood in God — and I recounted the story to him. He praised God, exalted is He, and set about expounding it. Now he had supposed in his mind that no one would attain to it; and when he heard that from me, he asked forgiveness of God, exalted is He, for that, and set about it, and named it al-Durr al-munaẓẓam fī ism Allāh al-aʿẓam ("The Well-Ordered Pearl, on the Greatest Name of God") — and it is [also] said, fī al-sirr al-aʿẓam ("on the Greatest Secret").

Then, after that, I saw the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — in another vision, and he was seated in the prayer-niche (miḥrāb), and the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — was present; and he was making mention of that tablet in the presence of the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace. And ʿAlī — may God ennoble his face — said: "The holy Name does not depend upon any other than itself for its signification." And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: "By the truth of the Truth, thus did Gabriel — peace be upon him — the Trustworthy Spirit, teach it to me." And when I recovered from my sleep, I came to the master (shaykh) and informed him of the vision; and he fell silent for the space of a full hour, then stretched out his hand behind his back and brought forth a slip of paper on which was written this very expression — I mean, "The holy, greatest

Name does not depend upon any other than itself for its signification." And when I saw that, I said to him: "Why do you not put it into the commentary?" He said: "I supposed that no one would come to know of it but myself, because of what had befallen me." Then he asked forgiveness of God, exalted is He, for that, as we mentioned at the first, and appended it to the commentary as we have set forth, and named it as we have described. And it is a secret among the secrets of God, exalted is He, which none attain save the truthful, who stand guard upon godfearing. For it is a mighty name and a noble secret: if you come to know the indication of its operative deployment (taṣrīf), mankind and the jinn will obey you, and the treasures will be opened to you — the treasures of knowledge and the treasures of the earth. So guard it from him who is not fit for it, and touch it not save when you are in a state of purity.

And this is its form, and it is as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, glorified and exalted, wills. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 40v./
Fig. 17

Know that the letters set in its angles are the letters of the triangle, and they are the completion of the nine numbers, which are the first letters of abjad, thus:(alif),(bāʾ),(jīm),(dāl),(hāʾ), (wāw), (zāy), (ḥāʾ),(ṭāʾ),(yāʾ) — and the yāʾ, the tenth of them, is in it for the vocative. So you say: Yā Allāh (O God), Yā Bāʿith (O Raiser of the dead), Yā Jalīl (O Majestic), Yā Dāʾim (O Everlasting), Yā Hādī (O Guide), Yā Wāḥid (O One), Yā Zakī (O Pure), Yā Ḥāfiẓ (O Preserver), Yā Ṭāhir (O Undefiled) — nine names that gather the nine letters. And [with them] what has already been given of the supplication, whose beginning is "O God, I ask You by [the truth] that You are God", to the end of it; and it is the supplication of this greatest figure.

And it is this noble supplication: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. O God, I ask You by [the truth] that You are God, sanctified by the properties proper to oneness (aḥadiyya) and to self-sufficiency (ṣamadiyya), above [having] an opposite, a peer, a contrary, or an equal; and by [the truth] that You are God, of whom there is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing (Q 42:11). I ask You to bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, and to the family of Muḥammad, and to everyone who loves Muḥammad; and to fulfil my need and all my needs, every one of them, and whatever holds for me the good of this world and of the hereafter, [I being] encompassed by [Your] watchful keeping, preserved from calamities, with the special marks of the [good] outcomes. O You who return again and again with good things! O You who are in reality worthy of pious reverence, worthy to forgive, and worthy of [bestowing] good things! O God, this is the request of a servant of the might of Your Lordship, in the making manifest of his request — for You are the Knower of the unseen realms, and the Witness of the reality of the seeker before /fol. 41r./ ever it comes into contact with hearts. So bring it to completion with a beautiful ending, O best of all that is sought. And may God bless our master Muḥammad, the beloved of hearts, and his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace." And this is the supplication of this greatest figure.

So draw the analogy and derive from it whatever you wish; and whatever you desire in it you will find, and you will attain your request in all that is hoped for. Sufficient is it as an utmost end! For it is the red sulphur (al-kibrīt al-aḥmar) and the greatest theriac (al-tiryāq al-akbar). So whoever understands its secret attains thereby what he desires, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

Another section of the same. He — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: I was in spiritual retreat (khalwa), and I saw a figure, namely a circle, and within the circle the Name of Majesty, which is Allāh. And there had branched off from it every name in which there is an ʿayn — and they are nineteen weighty names, which you see drawn in the figure, completing 20 with the Name of Majesty. And when this figure had become fixed in my mind, and that state had parted from me, and the luminous figure had been lifted away, I represented it upon paper. Then my thought returned to me, and I said: it is possible that I should bring forth from this name the ninety-nine names by way of branching. So I set about that, and a seizure took hold of me, and it was said to me:

— "Therein is thanksgiving for the making-known, together with the granting of success." So I asked forgiveness of God, exalted is He, and praised Him, and turned back from that thought which had occurred to me. These, then, are nineteen names that issued from the Name of Majesty (al-jalāla), and the Name of Majesty out of which they issued is the twentieth, which seals them. They possess benefits — things not to be doubted by anyone who knows how they are to be employed and has seen their efficacious influence. Among these: there is no matter, worldly or otherworldly, whose attainment a man desires — whereupon he purifies himself, faces the qibla, and prays two rakʿas in a clean place, in seclusion, with good intention and with fine recourse to God, exalted is He, at midnight or in the last part of it, and invokes these twenty names with presence of heart, in such a way that his thought is not occupied with anything other than the matter he is engaged upon, and recites them one thousand six hundred and seventy-three times (and if you wish to restrict yourself to fewer than that number, let it be one hundred and eighty-one times), and then asks God, glorified and exalted, for his need immediately after the supplication — but that God, exalted is He, makes its means easy for him; especially if he asks of God that some branch of knowledge be made easy for him, for God — mighty and majestic, exalted is He — opens for him from His mighty Name a road to his objective, and he sees therein marvels: some of them such as may be uttered, and some of them such as may not be uttered. Among these also: when a man writes this circle and places it among his goods, at home and on a journey, he is guarded, by the leave of God, exalted is He, from corrupters finding any way to him. And whoever writes it and hangs it upon his right upper arm and walks with it among his enemies, God, exalted is He, preserves him from them and forsakes them. And whoever goes in upon one of the tyrants whom he fears — that man is humbled before him and submits, and God, exalted is He, overturns his tyrannical might before him, and he is humbled before him and submits, and his soul is given over to what he desires, and he grants him his requests; and, by the leave of God, exalted is He, he is spared the evil of all that, because of the wondrous and majestic secrets contained in it. And if you write the noble names with rose-water, musk, saffron, and fine camphor, and give them as a draught to one in whose body there is a bodily ailment or a psychic ailment /fol. 41v./, it removes it and lightens it; and it gives its bearer strength in his soul, his body, and his spirit, and the names give him awe-inspiring presence and majesty, such that he witnesses that with a witnessing concerning which he has no doubt. And if a man invokes them every day after the dawn prayer seventy-seven times, and they become part of his litany, he will see, from the blessings of that, good things in his religion, his worldly life, and his soul — wondrous things, so much so that his aspiration scarcely ever attaches itself to any of the creatures, and the creatures are made subservient to him upon his completing them, and their love for him [is procured for him too]; and he loves them and they love him with an intense love. And if one of the tyrants wrongs a man, or overpowers him, or harms him, and he wishes to take vengeance upon him, let him recite this supplication and these names, saying: O God, O al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), O al-Sarīʿ (the Swift), O al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead), O al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator), O al-ʿAdl (the Just), O al-Muʿizz (the Giver of might), O al-Faʿʿāl (the Doer of what He wills) — in the first hour of Saturday, for the whole of it; and let him invoke against the one who wronged him and harmed him. For God, blessed and exalted, will take vengeance for him upon that man before the week comes round, and he will be granted victory over the one who wronged him.

And if you want it for love and for reconciliation between two who bear hatred toward each other, then the twenty names are written, and you write together with them the name of the one whom you wish to love you and to be subject to your command and your prohibition: so write his name and your name, dissolve them in water, and give the two who hate each other to drink of that water — they will come to love one another, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And likewise, if you give the names as a draught to whomever you wish, he will love you with an intense love and will never again wish to be parted from you. The writing is to be done in the daytime of Sunday, in the hour of the Sun or in the hour of Mercury, after you have suffumigated with a fragrant suffumigation such as aloeswood, nadd, ambergris, benzoin (jāwī), musk, nadd, and mastic. And that will come to pass, if God — exalted and glorified is He — wills.
And these are the twenty names alluded to. You say: O God, O al-Samīʿ, O al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), O al-Sarīʿ, O al-Wāsiʿ (the All-

Embracing), O al-ʿAdl, O al-ʿAlī (the Exalted), O al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), O al-Mutaʿāl (the Most High), O al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), O al-Bāʿith, O al-Faʿʿāl, O al-ʿAfū (the Pardoner), O al-Muʿīd (the Restorer), O al-Rafīʿ (the Sublime), O al-Maʿbūd (the Worshipped), O al-Māniʿ (the Withholder), O al-Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of benefit), O al-Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer), O al-Badīʿ. And this is the form of the Greatest Signet alluded to, and it is as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God — glorified and exalted is He, His be the praise — wills. And God, glorified and exalted, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 42r./
[Circular diagram (the Greatest Signet): as in the source — ]

And this is the supplication of the circle. You say: In the name of God, and with His name is the beginning made. In the name of God. O Lord, I ask You by Your name with which You opened the world of creation and of command, by the self-disclosure to the Real which makes manifest the relations of the sending-down; and [I ask You] by the One transcendent in command, in existence, and in an intelligible hiddenness — that being for whomever You have strengthened, nay, known to whomever You have granted witnessing, unknown to whomever You will — by reason of that in it which is ambiguous: a multiplicity that does no injury to the oneness of that which You have made firmly established of a firm decree. O al-ʿAlīm, O al-Ḥakīm (the Wise), O al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), O God, O Lord, I ask You, O God: O al-Samīʿ, O al-ʿAlīm, O al-Sarīʿ, O al-Wāsiʿ, O al-ʿAdl, O al-Mutaʿāl, O al-ʿAzīz, O al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving), O al-Bāʿith, O al-Shahīd (the Witness), O al-Rafīʿ, O al-Maʿbūd, O al-Māniʿ, O al-Muʿīd, O al-Rāfiʿ (the Raiser), O al-Mundafiʿ [so in the base text; perhaps read al-Mudāfiʿ, the Defender], O al-Jāmiʿ, O al-Badīʿ. I ask You, O God, by the secret of the relation (iḍāfa) that binds together the Presence of Necessity. I ask You, O God, by that which You have spread out in the malakūt (realm of dominion) of Your jabarūt (realm of omnipotence), and by that which You have made plain in the jabarūt of Your malakūt, and by that which You have kept to Yourself in the worlds of the holiness of Your lāhūt (realm of divinity), and by that which You have hidden from the apprehension of the intellects in the secret of the bahamūt of Your mercy, and by that which You have folded into the secret of Your secret in the ground of the well-proportioned existentiation, and by the symbols and the intimations which You have set out in detail among the kinds of the treasured modality within the inmost of the inmost depths of the descent: that You guard me with

Your impregnable guarding from the voices of Satan, his tunes, his promptings, and his slanders — for he makes good into evil, and land into sea, and sea into land /fol. 42v./, and benefit into harm — and from the ill-omen of his guile. I ask You, O God, that You bestow upon me, by Your all-pervading kindness and Your immense generosity, the rank of the kings luminous in bestowed graces (ʿawārif) and in operative deployment within the kingdom of acts; and honour me with Your perfect words in life and in death, that I may attain the glory of the paths of those bestowed graces; and bestow upon me from Yourself gnosis (ʿirfān), O Ḥannān (the Tender), O Mannān (the Bounteous), O Lord of the worlds.

Another faṣl belonging to it. It is that by which our master Jesus — upon him be peace and blessing — used to bring the dead to life, by the leave of God, exalted is He; and it is the Greatest Name. So know what has come to you of its good, that you may be made happy by it; for its secret is rare and its effect is wondrous. It is the name of God — the Mighty, the Great, the Greatest, the Good, the Pure, the Undefiled, the Complete, the Treasured, the Hidden — by which all the Most Beautiful Names are made to shine. Asad b. Mūsā transmitted it from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: This treasured, hidden Name — whoever writes it while fasting and with clean garment, on Sunday at sunrise, and suffumigates it with Indian aloeswood and red sandalwood, upon gazelle parchment or clean paper, and hangs it upon his forearm — good things hasten to him, and he witnesses of its blessing wondrous things not to be doubted. And this is the Name with which God sent Moses —

peace be upon him — to Pharaoh, when He said to him: Indeed I am God; there is no god but I, so worship Me (Q 20:14). And by this Name Zubayda held sway over Hārūn al-Rashīd, and he would do nothing save by her counsel and her opinion. And if you write it and suffumigate it close by the fire, and the writing is hung facing the sun, where it rises upon it and sets, and its rays do not leave it the whole day long, it becomes for him a means of acceptance among people.

And this is the supplication of the letter-circle, the expounded one, whose mention and whose excellence have gone before. You say: O God, I ask You — O God, O al-Qāhir (the Subduer), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), O al-Qāʾim (the Upholder), O al-Qadīr (the All-Powerful), O al-Quddūs (the All-Holy), O al-Qādir (the Powerful), O al-Qadīr, O al-Qarīb (the Near), O al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing) — You are the One who gave might to Your friends through Your prophets, and perfected Your prophets through the bearing of Your affliction, and crushed the wretched by the spreading out of the sovereignty of the dominion of Your power and of Your overmastering. I ask You by Your impregnable, momentous might, and by Your immense, all-powerful generosity, and by Your right over Your creation, over the exalted among them and the lowly, that You make me mighty among created beings through independence of them and neediness toward You; and honour me with Your life diffused within the secrets of their innermost selves, so that I may take refuge by it and turn toward You; and grant me a might drawn from Your ennobling of Your friends, in the final issue and in the present state, at Your drawing of them to Yourself; and make me mighty at the door of the Real through steadfastness and witnessing, that I may be one possessed of true selfhood (inniyya) before You; and spread out my might within the hearts of the people of faith, that I may attain the secret of Your compassion at the manifestation of the proof and the demonstration. O Ḥannān, O Mannān, You are the One who manifests in the hearts of those who love You the secret of the opening and of the self-disclosure. You hear what is subtler and more hidden, and with Your eye that neither sleeps nor slumbers You see the creeping of the black ant upon the solid rock, beneath the layers of the dust-coloured earth, in /fol. 43r./ the darkest night. O God, I ask You by the subtleties of what You have folded into hearing and sight; and by the fine things of what You have bestowed upon sight; and by the realities of what You have gathered together between hearing and sight; and by the fine points of what You have concealed within sight, that it might fall out in the place of hearing; and by the precedences of what You have hidden within hearing, that it might stand in the place of sight: that You grant me secrets folded into the encompassment of sight, and the witnessing of lights established at the containing of hearing and sight; and grant me, by Your luminosity and by the crowning of the secret of Your signs, the perpetuity of watchful vigilance over what descends from Your most high holiness, and the apprehensions of the All-Encompassing that gathers the names; and strengthen me to understand the calling of the soul to account with exacting reckoning. For You are the gatherer of every good and the repeller of every harm, O Lord of the worlds. I ask You, O God: O al-Qāhir, O al-Qahhār, O al-Qarīb, O al-Quddūs, O al-Qāʾim, O al-Qayyūm — I ask You to bless and grant peace to our master
